titulo: Myths about handling everything over text
hooks: Is texting customers enough to sell?
Handling everything by text has a limit
Answering the same questions all day long
voz: If they can text me, I don't need a website. On your website they already see hours, prices and location, and they reach out ready to buy. I reply fast, that's enough. At night you sleep, and your website keeps showing everything. A contact form will do. On a phone, a tap-to-text button is faster.

tarjetas.mito: If they can text me, I don't need a website
tarjetas.realidad: On your site they see hours, prices and location, and reach out ready to buy
At night you sleep, and your website keeps showing everything
On a phone, tapping a text button beats filling out a form

captions: Texting is great for closing a sale. But for someone to text you in the first place, they have to find you and trust you, and that happens on your website.
If you answer the same questions every day, put them on your website: hours, delivery area, payment options. Whoever reaches out after that is ready to buy.
When you're with a customer, asleep or on vacation, people can still see everything you offer on your website.
